title: Tirzepatide Efficacy and Tolerability According to Early Weight Response: A Post Hoc Analysis of the SURMOUNT-1 and SURMOUNT-2 Trials

what_it_measured.text: We aimed to assess weight reduction, CRPs, tolerability and hypoglycaemia according to early body weight response to tirzepatide in these studies.

Data from SM-1 and SM-2 tirzepatide-treated patients were categorized into two groups for the purpose of this analysis: early responders (≥ 5% weight reduction at Week 8) and nonearly responders (< 5% weight reduction at Week 8).

dose.text: Tirzepatide 2.5 mg (or matching placebo) was initiated once a week, and dose escalated every 4 weeks until the randomized dose of 5, 10 or 15 mg in SM-1 and 10 or 15 mg in SM-2 was achieved and continued until Week 72.

Week 8 of the study was used for categorization, as this time point represents a standardized treatment exposure at which all participants (from both SM-1 and SM-2) had been receiving tirzepatide 5 mg for 4 weeks and were scheduled for dose escalation to randomized dose [6].

endpoint.text: Outcomes were assessed using the efficacy estimand with logistic regression and mixed models for repeated measures.

All participants provided written informed consent. 2.2 | Outcomes To assess whether early body weight response was associated with varying degrees of body weight reduction, cardiometabolic risk parameters, tolerability and safety at Week 72, the following primary endpoints were analysed: percent change in body weight from baseline to Week 72 and proportion of participants who achieved weight reduction targets (≥5%, ≥10%, ≥15%, ≥20%, ≥25% and ≥30%) at Week 72.

reported_results.text: Results: Across both studies (N = 2384), ERs were more likely to be female, White and to have lower baseline HbA1c levels.

Post hoc exploratory analyses included tirzepatide-treated participants from SM-1 (n = 1775) and SM-2 (n = 609), categorized as early responders (ERs; ≥ 5% weight reduction) or nonearly responders (non-ERs; < 5% weight reduction) at Week 8.
In SM-1, females accounted for 67.5% of participants, with a mean age of 44.8 ± 12.3 years and were mostly White (70.3%).
3 | Results 3.1 | Participants Of the tirzepatide-treated participants in SM-1 and SM-2 trials, data from 2384 participants were analysed.
The difference was more evident at higher body weight reduction targets (≥ 15% and above; Figure 1E,F).
At Week 72, weight reduction in SM-1 was −23.3% ± 0.3% in early responders and −14.6% ± 0.4% in nonearly responders (p < 0.001).
